title: how the moves-together signal reaches gs without going through the index
summary: The "Moves together" pairs shown by gs are NOT part of the code index and never travel through the cache pipeline — they live in a separate keeper-written sidecar (cochange.json) that each reader loads itself and hands to handleGetStructure as a THIRD argument. This is why gs can show them at all: handleGetStructure is synchronous and takes only an index, so there was no way to reach git from inside it. Consequence for anyone adding a similar signal: don't try to hang it off CodebaseIndex — the cache is consumer-scoped and gzip-swept, and a reader that already has an index still needs a second explicit load. It also means a surface that forgets to pass the argument silently renders nothing rather than erroring.
